findings.title: Device ID is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice, allowing device limit bypass on subsequent requests
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` on line 87 before calling `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` on line 93. When the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request fails authentication, but the rejected `deviceID` remains in `localCache` for 29 minutes. On the very next request with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id`, `a.localCache.Get(key)` on line 83 hits the cache and `tagDeviceUI` returns `nil`, allowing the over-limit device to authenticate without ever being persisted or counted. Cache insertion should only happen after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

findings.title: MySQL RowsAffected() returns 0 on no-op UPDATE, falsely triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached for existing devices
findings.body: In `updateDevice`, when the device limit is reached and an already-registered device makes a request within the same second (MySQL `DATETIME` has 1-second precision and Grafana does not enable `clientFoundRows` on the MySQL DSN), `updated_at`, `client_ip`, and `user_agent` are identical to the stored row. MySQL's `RowsAffected()` returns 0 when matched rows have no changed column values, causing line 95 (`if rowsAffected == 0`) to return `ErrDeviceLimitReached` for a valid, already-counted device.

findings.title: Changed ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature without regenerating Wire DI code
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changed its parameter from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB`, and `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` changed from `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB)` to `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB, deviceLimit int64)`. Neither `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` nor the Wire provider sets in `pkg/server/wire.go` were updated in this PR, which will break the build.
